   Cato Networks is the converged network and security cloud for the AI era.     
  As AI reshapes cybersecurity, enterprises face a dual challenge: unlocking AI’s potential while defending against AI-driven attacks. Cato addresses both through a unified, cloud-native platform, providing the visibility and context to prioritize risks and stop threats in real time across users, applications, data, and AI agents.     
  Join us as we scale: take on ambitious technological challenges and shape the next generation of enterprise security at a company trusted by thousands of organizations worldwide.     
     Cato Networks is seeking a NOC Engineer to join the team. In this critical role, you will be monitoring, supporting, and providing advanced troubleshooting of a large complex data network infrastructure by using network monitoring and management tools. You will work closely with teams from our business areas, network engineering, and management as a team representative on major incident bridges. This is a remote position based in the Philippines.   Key Responsibilities  
 
 Own and manage the uptime, stability, and overall functionality of the company’s production systems. This includes troubleshooting and resolving system and network issues end-to-end. 
 Monitor and respond to NetOps alerts during working hours, and review/follow up on alerts triggered outside business hours as required. 
 Continuously track and analyze system performance to identify risks, bottlenecks, capacity constraints, and opportunities for optimization. 
 Proactively mitigate outages and system malfunctions to prevent customer impact. When necessary, prepare clear and prioritized escalations to the relevant Development teams. 
 Coordinate with third-party service providers (e.g., carriers, SMS providers, IX providers, and other vendors) to resolve network and system-related issues. 
 Provide advanced (higher-tier) technical support to internal Customer Support teams (T1–T3). 
 Design, implement, and maintain dashboards and alerting mechanisms to ensure system visibility and operational awareness. 
 Serve as a technical focal point for Customer Support and Field Engineering teams by understanding business use cases and translating them into operational requirements. 
 Contribute to building, improving, and expanding NetOps ownership, processes, documentation, and operational best practices. 
 
  Role Scope  
 
 The role is primarily driven by automated system alerts requiring investigation, troubleshooting, and escalation when necessary. 
 The role also involves handling customer-impacting issues escalated by the Customer Support organization. 
 In addition to reactive tasks, the position includes ongoing projects and operational initiatives to be managed during working hours. 
 
  Required Skills & Experience  
 
 Strong experience in network architecture, cloud architecture, and security architecture. 
 Deep knowledge of TCP/IP networking, routing, firewalls, proxy servers, and related technologies. 
 Strong ability to analyze system and application logs to identify root causes of issues. 
 Advanced troubleshooting and problem-solving skills with the ability to diagnose complex network and system incidents. 
 Experience working in a Cloud or SaaS technology environment. 
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly document findings and communicate with cross-functional teams. 
 Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and manage multiple concurrent projects and incidents simultaneously.

jobs.description:
Headquarters:

   Our Commitment to Our Team  
 At Pipe17, our values aren’t just words on a wall. They’re how we operate every day. 
 We are a high-performance team built around  ownership ,  urgency ,  curiosity , and a strong  bias for action . 
 We set bold goals, hold ourselves accountable, and move fast to solve customer problems. Every team member owns their decisions and drives outcomes. No one waits for permission. 
 We operate with  urgency , but not recklessly. We focus on what matters most, take initiative, and course-correct quickly when needed. We value people who speak up, follow through, and take pride in their work. 
  Curiosity  is how we get better. We ask questions, challenge assumptions, and stay open to new ideas. We don’t default to “how it’s always been done.” We explore, test, and learn. That mindset helps us adapt quickly, solve harder problems, and continuously raise the bar. 
 We also embrace  AI as a force multiplier . We believe great operators don’t compete with AI - they partner with it. We use AI to move faster, think deeper, and remove friction from our work, while still applying human judgement, creativity, and context where it matters most. Thoughtful use of AI is part of how we scale ourselves and our impact. 
  Finally, teamwork  is at our core. We win together, support each other, and celebrate our shared victories. Collaboration across functions is a daily practice, not just something we talk about. We learn from each other, improve constantly, and rally around our mission: unify commerce after the buy button. 
 If these values resonate with how you like to work, you’ll fit right in.    Type:  Individual Contributor ·  Location:  Remote (US) ·  Reports to:  VP Marketing  Experience:  3–5 years ·  Target OTE:  $105k–$115k 
 This is a hands-on build role, and acts as the connective tissue to our cross-functional GTM team. You will work daily with Sales and Partnerships, because the programs you build feed their pipeline across mid-market brands, enterprise order management, and 3PL. 
 About the role 
 Pipe17’s Order Operations Platform is the connected OMS that unifies orders, inventory, products and fulfillment across selling channels (DTC, B2B, retail and agentic), ERPs and fulfillment locations. We sell a technical product to operators, their bosses and the rest of the enterprise buying group, and generic marketing does not work on them. 
 We need someone who can build the systems that put the right message in front of the right account at the right moment, then run those systems without babysitting. You are part engineer, part marketer: comfortable in APIs, automation platforms, and LLM tooling, and equally comfortable judging whether a play will actually grow qualified pipeline. You will be the only person in this function, reporting directly to the VP of Marketing, with the latitude to build what does not exist yet. 
 What you'll do 
  Run account-based marketing execution.  
 
 Build the named account lists for our enterprise and 3PL programs, and map the people inside each account. 
 Keep account evidence current, built with agents rather than by hand: what each account runs, who runs it, what it costs them, and what changed. 
 Run the mechanics: multi-touch sequences, executive outreach, dinner and event invitations, gifting, and follow-up. 
 Own event and conference follow-up as a system. Target list and meetings booked before anyone travels, follow-up inside 72 hours. 
 Give Sales and Partnerships what they need to work each account, when they need it. 
 
  Build custom nurtures.  Replace the single nurture track with custom paths, where treatment rises with intent and decays with time. High-intent visitors get a human fast, light engagement gets agent-drafted outreach keyed to what they did, and stalled or previously-too-small accounts get re-scored and re-contacted on a schedule. 
  Own HubSpot.  Own the roadmap and the admin. Fix the data model so it matches how we actually sell across three segments, clean up source attribution so we can say what produced pipeline, and build reporting the business trusts. Keep the stack small. We are not looking for someone who adds tools. 
  Build the outbound engine.  
 
 Build automated outbound end to end: signal detection, enrichment, sequencing, reply handling, and CRM sync, using the tools we have in house today (HubSpot, Clay, Propensity, Artisan, Gong). 
 Detect the events that mean an account is in play: a replatform, an ERP migration, a 3PL change, a new channel, a second warehouse, a bad peak season, a new operations or technology leader. 
 Use LLMs and agents to personalize at volume, grounded in real research about each account. 
 Make it run without babysitting, and make it measurable. 
 
 Must-have qualifications 
 
 3+ years in marketing operations, demand gen operations, GTM operations, or revenue operations at a B2B

jobs.description:
Who are we?  
  Tripledot  Studios  is one of the largest independent mobile games companies in the world. 
 We are a multi-award-winning organisation, with a global 2,500+ strong team across 12 studios. 
 Our expanded portfolio includes some of the biggest titles in mobile gaming, collectively reaching top chart positions around the world and engaging over 25 million daily active users. 
 Tripledot’s guiding principle is that when people love what they do, what they do will be loved by others. 
 We’re building a company we’re proud of. One filled with driven, incredibly smart and detail-orientated people, who  LOVE  making games. 
 Our ambition is to be the most successful games company in the world, and we’re just getting started. 
  This role sits within our Peoplefun studio.  PeopleFun is an award-winning creator of mobile games for players across the globe, and a part of  Tripledot Studios , with world-class projects, resources, and infrastructure.   PeopleFun is a Dallas-based game studio founded and led by game industry veterans, where game developers thrive on collaboration, creativity, teamwork, and fun. Our games are played by over 25 million players each month, and we are hard at work on a number of exciting new mobile games to fuel our future growth.  We believe in bringing People together through Fun by creating best-in-class social features and communities in our games that enable our players to engage deeply with other players. We also bring our studio teammates together by creating the very best game teams, ones that foster healthy collaboration, incredible productivity, and life-long professional relationships.  Job Summary  Wordscapes is one of the most-loved word puzzle games on mobile, and a long-running live game with a huge, loyal player base. We're looking for a Senior Game Designer who can do two things really well: craft levels players can't put down, and design features that keep them coming back for years.  You'll own work end to end, from the first idea and spec through ABT, tuning and live ops. Some weeks that means reshaping the early level ramp so new players stick around longer. Other weeks it means designing a new event, meta system or level mechanic and seeing it in front of millions of players. You'll sit on a small, senior, data-literate team where good ideas ship fast and every change is measured.

 Design, build and tune crossword levels and level ramps, balancing word choice, grid layout, letter sets and difficulty. 
 Shape progression and pacing across hundreds of levels, with deliberate spikes, breathers and rewards. 
 Use per-level funnels, churn points and completion data to find where players struggle, then fix it. 
 Design new level mechanics and goals that add variety and depth without breaking the core loop. 
 Partner with engineers on tooling, procedural generation, and general collaboration. 
  Feature design  
 Own features end to end: pitch, spec, UX flows, reward tuning, and success metrics. 
 Design retention-focused systems for new, engaged and returning lapsed players, from FTUE to long-term meta. 
 Write clear features specs with a hypothesis, treatments and KPIs, then read results with data partners and decide next steps. 
 Work closely with product, engineering, art, UX and QA to get features shipped on time and at quality. 
  Across both  
 Prototype ideas quickly, on paper, in whitebox, or with AI tools, and drop what doesn't test well. 
 Play the top casual and word games and bring back sharp, specific lessons. 
 Bring your years of experience and expertise to raise the bar for design docs and reviews on the team. 
  Requirements  
 5+ years of game design experience, with at least 3 years on mobile casual or puzzle games. 
 Hands-on level design: you've built, tuned and shipped levels at scale in a level editor, and can show examples. 
 Feature design: you've taken features from concept to live, and can walk us through what moved the metrics and what didn't. 
 Strong grasp of progression, pacing, difficulty curves, FTUE and retention levers. 
 Comfortable working from data: funnels, cohorts, retention curves and A/B test results. 
 Clear, structured writing. Your specs are easy for engineers, artists and QA to build from. 
 Experience working in a live game with regular releases and live ops. 
 This role is remote, with a hybrid schedule for those near our Dallas office: 4 days a week in office (Monday–Thursday) if you live in Dallas, or 3 days a week (Monday–Wednesday) if you live within a 3-hour radius.

 Shipped word, crossword, puzzle or match-3 games. 
 Hands-on with Looker, BigQuery, Tableau or similar, enough to answer your own questions. 
 Designing ABTs on level content: difficulty, ramps, content swaps. 
 Spreadsheet fluency for ramp, economy and parameter tables. 
 Unity experience. 
 Procedural or AI-assisted content generation. 
 Prototypes or tools you've built with AI.

jobs.description:
Headquarters:  Las Vegas, Nevada, United States
      URL:   https://www.skillz.com 
 

  About Beamable   
 Beamable is the backend and LiveOps infrastructure platform for game developers, the system that lets studios build, operate, and scale live games without constructing the underlying architecture themselves. Backend services, identity, analytics, meta-game systems, virtual economies, and AI-native tooling: all integrated into a single platform that eliminates the point-solution stitching that has defined game development for too long. Beamable also powers Wingman, an agentic LiveOps product that gives game teams a unified operating system to understand, optimize, and act on live game performance in real time. This is the future of how games are operated. 
 Beamable is part of  FIRY , a founder-led global technology portfolio operating at the intersection of gaming, AI-powered performance marketing, and developer infrastructure. Acquired in January 2026, and together with Skillz, our competition platform, and  RZR , our AI-driven  ad  network, Beamable sits at the foundation of a compounding ecosystem that no standalone competitor can replicate. If you want to build the infrastructure that games run on at a company with the vision and resources to back it — Beamable is the right place to do it. 
  About the Role   
 Beamable is seeking a Head of Product to shape its platform vision and lead its next phase of growth in the game backend market. This is an opportunity to build the product function from the ground up, guide the platform from early access through public release, and advance AI integration to deliver meaningful value for game studios. 
 As the company’s senior product leader and sole product practitioner, you will own product strategy, roadmap, launch milestones, and success metrics, combining strategic direction with hands-on execution. You will work directly with studios and design partners, represent Beamable’s product vision at industry events, and translate customer insights into clear priorities. Success in this role means delivering a successful public launch, developing early-access studios into reference customers, and establishing a product foundation that drives adoption and sustained revenue growth. 
  Responsibilities   
 
   Product Strategy & Vision Ownership.  Set the product vision for Beamable’s platform — spanning player engagement, developer tools, data enrichment, and player intelligence — and own the roadmap from early access through public release and beyond. Partner with the  CRO  on packaging, pricing, and tracking the studio funnel quantitatively. 
  Public Release & Launch Execution.  Drive Beamable’s product through its launch milestones: early design partners, public release, and strategic partnerships. Define and own the go/no-go criteria for each milestone, ensuring the product ships when it’s ready to win. 
  Studio Partnership & Customer Discovery.  Spend meaningful time every week with studios, design partners, and game developers — running discovery calls, demos, onboarding sessions, and roadmap reviews. Join sales calls and paid pilots with the  CRO  and turn each design partner into a reference case. 
  AI Integration & Product Intelligence.  Define the guardrails, data policies, and feedback loops that make Beamable’s AI capabilities safe, effective, and trustworthy for game teams. Integrate with best-in-class tools studios already use and shape the intelligent systems that differentiate the platform. 
  Metrics Ownership & Product Function Build-Out.  Define success metrics across the studio lifecycle — time to value, pilot conversion, retention, usage, and revenue per studio — and do your own analysis in SQL. Establish the product processes Beamable runs on: discovery, specs, prioritization, and launch reviews. 
 
   
   
  Key Competencies  
 
  Platform Product Strategy.  Proven ability to set and execute product vision for a developer-facing platform, owning the strategy across multiple capability areas simultaneously — not just a feature set.

  AI/ML Product Judgment.  Experience shipping AI or ML-driven features to production. Knows where AI adds genuine value, where it needs guardrails, and how to define data policies that serve both studio needs and platform integrity. 
  Data Fluency & Metrics Ownership.  Can build dashboards, write SQL, and live with retention, churn, and revenue metrics over time. Runs experiments before big bets rather than after.
